commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(`ls /workspace/*/bifrost` finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes
and is checked out detached at this exact commit: 0722dea6bcb52ef5335695a701631d157c31cbf4
Do not fetch from origin or any other remote.
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

History rule. Work only from the base commit above. Do not log, show, diff, check
out or otherwise read any commit, branch or tag that is not an ancestor of the base,
and do not use gh, the GitHub API or the web for this issue, its comments, timeline
or pull requests: the issue text in this brief is complete.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.
If the build cache wrapper stalls (a cargo command that starts no compiler for
more than ten minutes), you may run that command through plain cargo
(/usr/local/cargo/bin/cargo) and say so in your report; do not move target/
or change shared cache settings.

regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.

 the #2904 benchmark case `pond-stopped-flag` (pond commit c0b34be) still reports its real race as open with `unresolved_target`. The race row names these unresolved calls (the `unresolved_calls` field on concurrency rows):

| pond.go line | Call | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 111 | `Eager()`, a function in another file of the same package | dynamic_or_incomplete_dispatch |
| 117 | `opt(pool)`, a function value from a variadic slice | dynamic_or_incomplete_dispatch |
| 136 | `Context(context.Background())(pool)`, a returned function value | dynamic_or_incomplete_dispatch |
| 380 | `idleTicker.Stop()`, receiver typed by `time.NewTicker`'s result | dynamic_or_incomplete_dispatch |
| 461 | `p.strategy.Resize(...)`, an interface method | dynamic_or_incomplete_dispatch |

Across pond, ants, cache2go and workerpool, `dynamic_or_incomplete_dispatch` accounts for 1,989 named unresolved-call occurrences, against about 900 for all unmodeled library calls together. It is the largest single reason the race analysis cannot prove a race.

Line 380 is the case bc9ec425e addresses in the resolver, and it is still unresolved in race analysis. That suggests the new resolution does not yet reach semantic lowering.

## Where race analysis reads targets

- Go semantic lowering sets a call's declared targets in `lower_call_operands` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/go/semantic.rs). A same-file method selector is resolved there; other shapes fall through to Unknown with a dispatch gap.
- An incomplete workspace dispatch becomes `UnresolvedTarget` in the race provider (crates/bifrost-rql/src/structural/search/concurrency.rs).

## Request

Include Go semantic lowering's call targets (and the workspace dispatch the concurrency provider uses) in the native Go cutover, or record why they stay on the incumbent path. The pond lines above are ready-made acceptance cases: run `bifrost_benchmark go-race run --case pond-stopped-flag` and check that the 216/355 row's `unresolved_calls` shrinks.

Related: #2900 (Go race epic), #2904 (benchmark).

FINAL REPORT

Both witnesses are fixed: pond lines 380 (`idleTicker.Stop()`) and 111 (`Eager()`) no longer appear in the 216/355 row's `unresolved_calls`. Semantic lowering did not need to change, and the cause was not a routing gap. The new regression tests and the affected suites pass. Three failures are pre-existing, and I reproduced all three on a clean base worktree. Two points need your judgement: I changed the embedded Go declaration pack, and the build wrapper stalled once (details below).

## 1. Confirmed cause

- **Lowering is per-file by construction.** `lower_call_operands` (`go/semantic.rs`) can only set `declared_targets` to a `ProcedureId`, which names a procedure in one file's artifact. It already handles a function literal, a stable local binding, an interface proof, and a same-file package function or method. Cross-file and external targets come from `PreparedWorkspaceDispatchSession::resolve_call` (`semantic/workspace_oracle/dispatch.rs`), which asks the definition resolver. The race provider's `exact_model_summary` (`concurrency.rs`) only reads that outcome.
- **bc9ec425e never reached race analysis.** `GoSupport::native_rollout_points` and `go_native_external_receiver_call_resolution` are compiled only under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`, and `native_call_relations.rs` says Go call relations stay on the incumbent route until the flip. Race analysis already used the incumbent resolver through dispatch. So the issue's "does not reach lowering" premise does not hold at this base.
- **Line 380 was a data gap.** I reproduced it in a small package with the base binary using RQL `dispatch_outcome`: outcome `unknown`, coverage `open`, zero targets. The embedded `go-concurrency-declarations` pack declared `time.Timer`, `time.Time`, `time.Duration` and `AfterFunc`, but not `time.Ticker` or `time.NewTicker`. `NewTicker` had no result type, so the selector resolved to nothing. The reviewed summaries for `time.NewTicker` and `time.Ticker.Stop` already shipped and could not bind. A `time.AfterFunc` timer's `Stop` resolved in the same fixture.
- **Line 111 was a different cause.** `Eager` is `var Eager = func() ResizingStrategy {...}` in resizer.go, not a function. `dispatch_targets` returned `pond._module_.Eager` (kind `field`) as an `unmaterialized` boundary with proof proven and completeness partial; `procedure_matches_definition` requires `definition.is_callable()`. `Plain()` (a real function in the same other file) already resolved, so cross-file same-package resolution works.

## 2. Changes and reasons

Base `0722dea6bcb52ef5335695a701631d157c31cbf4`; final `2fae832bea66a3de373840dabd4bcc1d77dc9f9d`, in four commits: `723600f9f8`, `58e77da1ba`, `d766ebe7fd`, `2fae832bea`.

- **Declaration pack.** Added `time.Ticker`, `time.NewTicker`, `Ticker.Stop` and `Ticker.Reset` to `models/go-concurrency-declarations.json`, with my own regenerated shards and manifest. IDs were checked against all 55 existing ones. The `lib.rs` census went from 16/39 to 17/42 types/members, and the Timer lookups became owner-aware.
- **`brokk-bifrost-go` `callable_variable.rs`.** Two tree-sitter predicates: which function literal a package variable's declaration holds (one name, one value), and whether a file can write the variable (assignment, range or receive target, `++`/`--`, or `&`, by identifier or selector field). A file with a syntax error never qualifies.
- **`analyzer/go/callable_variable.rs` and `dispatch.rs`.** The analyzer-side wrapper checks every file from `ImportGraphCandidateProvider` (declaring file, directory siblings, direct importers). Dispatch then keeps the literal's procedure with the resolver's own proof. If any file might write the variable, nothing is retained and the call stays open.
- **Epoch bump: none.** I judged that no persisted language facts changed: the pack is a declaration overlay and the dispatch change is query-time. Say so if you read that differently.

t at this base, so bc9ec425e could not reach it. Semantic lowering stays file-local, because a procedure ID names a procedure of one file's artifact. The two pond calls failed for different reasons. `idleTicker.Stop()` had no target because the Go declaration pack declared `time.Timer` but not `time.Ticker` or `time.NewTicker`, so the receiver had no type. `Eager()` is a package variable holding a function literal, so the resolver returned a declaration with no body. The fix adds the four Ticker declarations and lets dispatch use a package variable's function literal when its declaration is one literal and no file that can reference it writes or takes the address of it. On the pond case the 216/355 row goes from seven open calls to five, and lines 111 and 380 are resolved. Across the pond, ants, cache2go and workerpool cases no row changes proof or gains an open call, and open dispatch occurrences fall by 26 to 30 in pond and ants. Function values, interface calls with several implementations, and any reassignable variable stay open, and tests pin those near misses. The native cutover therefore needs to supply the same two facts where dispatch asks the resolver, not in `lower_call_operands`. `time.NewTimer` and `context` models remain separate follow-ups.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A race-analysis "unresolved call" is only reported when it lies in the slice of one of the two conflicting accesses. My first tests passed before the fix because the unresolved calls sat outside that slice, so the tests had to mimic pond's shape exactly to fail before the fix.
- The Go lowering can't name cross-file targets because `ProcedureId` is artifact-local. That is why the cross-file fix lives in the dispatch layer, and why the native cutover has to supply the same two facts there.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
